subject: Coordinating multi-region POC kickoff & rotating hands-on sessions
messages:
From: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@acme-fin.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Cc: Diego Ruiz <diego.ruiz@acme-fin.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 13:15:00 +0000
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - multi-region schedule

Hi Aisha / Jonas,

Thanks again for the demo yesterday — the team at Acme is eager to get the hands-on sessions scheduled. We have three key objectives for the POC kickoff week: prompt review and tuning, routing/variant fallbacks, and a short load run to validate throughput.

Constraints from our side:
- US engineering can do mornings PT (08:00–11:00 PT).
- EU product leads prefer 14:00–18:00 CET.
- APAC SREs are only reliably available in their evening (20:00–23:00 SGT).

Instead of a single long block, we would prefer 3 shorter focused sessions (60–90m) rotated so the same Redwood engineers don't have to be on at 2am repeatedly. Can you propose a rotating schedule that hits each region's preferred window?

Also: what do you need from us ahead of the session for the load run (test tokens, sample prompt set, target qps)? Happy to loop Diego (SRE) into any prep docs.

Cheers,
Sam
Sam Lewis
Head of Platform Engineering | Acme Financial
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 18:02:00 +0000
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - multi-region schedule

Sam — thanks, this is helpful.

Proposed approach (short bullets so we can iterate quickly):
1) Three rotating 75-minute working sessions during the week:
   - Session A (US-friendly): 08:30–09:45 PT — prompt review + routing walkthrough
   - Session B (EU-friendly): 15:00–16:15 CET — configuration + canary/fallback test
   - Session C (APAC-friendly): 20:30–21:45 SGT — short load run + post-mortem
2) Rotation plan: each Redwood tech lead (Jonas/Tessa/Marissa) takes a different session slot each day so no single person repeats late-night shifts.
3) Prep asks from Acme before the load run: sample prompt set (500–1k prompts), expected concurrency/QPS target, and a list of test accounts to avoid touching production.

I attached a draft agenda (acme-poc-multizone-agenda.pdf) and a calendar-poll.ics with the three slot templates. Please confirm who from Acme will own the prep items. Once you confirm, I'll send invites and CC the relevant Redwood on-call.

Quick note on resources: we can reserve a small Dedicated pool for the load run to get predictable throughput; Jonas, can you confirm sizing?

Thanks — Aisha

Aisha Rahman
Senior Solutions Lead | Redwood Inference
[aisha_rahman@redwood.ai]
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Sam Lewis <sam.lewis@acme-fin.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:20:00 +0100
Subject: Re: POC kickoff - multi-region schedule

On Thu, 12 Mar 2026 at 18:02 +0000, Aisha Rahman wrote:
> I attached a draft agenda ... please confirm who from Acme will own the prep items.

Thanks — I'll size the Dedicated pool for the load run. My quick estimate for a short validation run (30m sustained) is:
- Target qps: 25–50 (depends on average token length)
- Recommended reserve: 2x expected qps headroom for safety during warmup
- Suggested run: three 10-minute buckets at increasing load (20/40/60 qps) to check steady-state and latency tail.

Tessa — can you join the APAC session for the load execution and SRE handoff?

Sam — to answer your prep list: a CSV of ~1k prompts and a test user namespace is ideal. If you can drop the prompts in the Drive folder I linked, we will pull them into our harness. Also suggest we run one dry run during Session A (US slot) with a subset to validate tool-calling and prompt formatting.

Calendar poll: https://doodle.com/poll/REDWOOD-ACME-POC (placeholder)
Drive prep folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/u/0/folders/1A2bAcme-POC

-Jonas
Lead Inference Engineer | Redwood Inference

- APAC folks noted that 20:30 SGT is borderline but manageable once a rotation is confirmed — happy to run that session when needed.
- For the EU slot, can we shift 15:00 CET -> 14:30 CET? That gives us a slightly earlier window for EU product to share screens before their end of day.
- I'll own the invites for customer-facing attendees and include a short pre-read (1 pager) so the product leads can come prepared.

Attached: load-test-plan.xlsx (high level), and I'll add a short attendee roster to the Drive folder.
